bib.title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning

read.skipped: Reference list (about chars 41511-80299) skimmed only; datasheet tables 14-16 and model card lightly read (checked for sizes and licences).

question: Can a model that bridges a frozen vision encoder and a frozen large LM, trained on web interleaved image-text data, learn new vision-language tasks from a handful of in-context examples?
hypothesis: Training on arbitrarily interleaved web image-text data with frozen pretrained components gives in-context few-shot ability on image and video tasks without task-specific tuning.
contributions: Flamingo family of VLMs accepting interleaved visual and text input and producing free-form text
Quantitative few-shot evaluation on 16 benchmarks, with a held-out set not used for design decisions
New few-shot SotA on 16 tasks; beats fine-tuned SotA on 6 with 32 examples; fine-tuning sets SotA on five more

method.summary: Frozen NFNet-F6 vision encoder (contrastively pretrained) feeds a Perceiver Resampler producing 64 visual tokens; new gated cross-attention dense layers (tanh gate init 0) are interleaved into a frozen Chinchilla LM (1.4B, 7B, 70B). Trained on M3W, ALIGN, LTIP and VTP with a weighted next-token loss; evaluated by in-context prompting on 16 benchmarks.
method.task: visually conditioned next-token prediction; few-shot in-context evaluation

datasets.name: M3W (MultiModal MassiveWeb)
datasets.size: about 43 million webpages; datasheet: 43.3M documents, 185M images, 182 GB text
datasets.split: random subsequence of L=256 tokens per document, up to first N=5 images
datasets.source: scraped web pages, English only, internal explicit-content filters; proprietary
datasets.preprocessing: <image> tags inserted at image positions, <EOC> before each image and at end; images <64px or aspect ratio >3 dropped; p_next=0.5 image-index augmentation

datasets.name: ALIGN
datasets.preprocessing: <image> prepended, <EOC> appended; avg 12.4 tokens per text; deduplicated against benchmarks

datasets.name: LTIP (Long Text & Image Pairs)
datasets.source: crawled from fewer than ten websites; proprietary

datasets.name: VTP (Video & Text Pairs)
datasets.size: 27 million short videos, about 22 s on average
datasets.source: crawled; none from YouTube or Flickr
datasets.preprocessing: 8 frames at 1 FPS per clip in training; not deduplicated

datasets.name: 16 evaluation benchmarks (COCO, OKVQA, VQAv2, MSVDQA, VATEX = DEV; Flickr30k, VizWiz, TextVQA, VisDial, HatefulMemes, MSRVTTQA, iVQA, YouCook2, RareAct, NextQA, STAR)
datasets.size: DEV eval: 5000 COCO samples, 1024 VATEX and QA samples; support sets 2048 samples
datasets.split: validation support/query and test support/query for DEV; ImageNet and Kinetics700 also used as DEV classification: 10 images/class, 32 support per class

models.name: Flamingo-3B
models.params: 3.2B total (1.4B frozen LM, 435M vision, 1.2B trainable xattn, 194M resampler)
models.architecture: frozen Chinchilla LM + GATED XATTN-DENSE before every block

other.table4_note: text says 1.4B additional learned params, Table 5 says 1.2B

models.name: NFNet-F6 contrastive vision encoder
models.architecture: NFNet-F6 with BERT text encoder, CLIP two-term loss

other.steps: 1.2 million (2 gradient calcs each) on 512 TPUv4
other.clip: AGC 1e-2 on NFNet, global norm 10 on BERT

training.objective: weighted sum over datasets of next-token negative log-likelihood of text given visuals, lambda: M3W 1.0, ALIGN 0.2, LTIP 0.2, VTP 0.03; gradients accumulated across datasets
training.lr_schedule: linear from 0 to 1e-4 over first 5000 steps then constant
training.seq_len: 256 tokens per M3W sample, up to 5 images
training.precision: trained params and optimizer state float32; activations and gradients bfloat16; frozen params bfloat16
training.regularisation: random flips and colour augmentation; space prepended to paired text with prob 0.5

other.ablation_setup: Flamingo-3B, batch 256 M3W, 512 ALIGN, 512 LTIP, 64 VTP; 1M gradient steps = 250,000 updates
other.finetune: LM frozen, vision encoder unfrozen, 480x480, per-task grid search lr 3e-8 to 1e-5, batch 8 or 16
other.video: 8 frames at 1 FPS in training; 30 frames at 3 FPS at inference via interpolated temporal embeddings
other.framework: JAX and Haiku, Megatron sharding, ZeRO stage 1

inference.decoding: beam search, beam size 3, open-ended; log-likelihood ranking for close-ended; greedy for qualitative
inference.samples: single trained model; support examples ordered randomly; ensembling over 6 random permutations of few-shot examples
inference.prompting: Question: {question} Answer: {answer} for QA; Output: {output} for others; up to 32 shots; zero-shot uses two text-only examples; VisDial capped at 16 shots
inference.retrieval: RICES: nearest support images by frozen encoder features, ordered by increasing similarity

metrics.name: VQA accuracy
metrics.definition: VQA acc of Antol et al.

metrics.name: Overall score
metrics.definition: each DEV benchmark score divided by its Table 1 SotA, averaged over 5 DEV benchmarks (validation, 4 shots)

eval.protocol: single hyperparameter set across benchmarks; 11 benchmarks held out of design decisions; no repeats or error bars

prompts.text: is an image with written: "{meme_text}" on it. Is it hateful? Answer: {answer}
This is a conversation between a human, User, and an intelligent visual AI, Flamingo. User sends images, and Flamingo describes them.
prompts.where: App B.1.6 (continues with three example turns)

evidence.quote: The learning rate is increased linearly from 0 to 10−4 up over the ﬁrst 5000 steps then held constant

results.claim: Flamingo-80B at 32 shots beats the fine-tuned state of the art on 6 of 16 benchmarks with about 1000x less task-specific data
results.setup: Flamingo-80B, 32 in-context examples, no weight updates; 15 comparable tasks since RareAct has no fine-tuned result
results.note: Table 1 caption says 'seven tasks'; text, Fig 2 and model card say 6
results.quote: On 6 of these 16 tasks, Flamingo also outperforms the ﬁne-tuned state of the art despite using only 32 task-speciﬁc examples, around 1000 times less task-speciﬁc training data

results.claim: VQAv2 test-dev, Flamingo-80B 32-shot
results.setup: Flamingo-80B, 32 shots, VQAv2 test-dev, VQA accuracy; DEV benchmark
results.note: App B.2.2 prints the 32-shot figure as 67.3%
results.table: Table 1, row Flamingo 32 shot, column VQAv2

results.claim: Fine-tuned Flamingo-80B on VQAv2 test-dev beats previous SotA
results.setup: Flamingo-80B fine-tuned per task, vision encoder unfrozen, 480x480, VQAv2 test-dev
results.quote: on VQAv2, we observe improved results at 82.0%, outperforming our results achieved with 32-shot in-context learning (67.3%) as well as the previous state of the art (81.3%, Yan et al. [133])

results.claim: Flamingo-80B zero-shot VQAv2 test-dev
results.setup: Flamingo-80B, 0 shots (two text-only examples), VQAv2 test-dev
results.table: Table 1, row Flamingo 0 shot, column VQAv2

results.claim: Freezing the LM beats fine-tuning it: fine-tuning a pretrained LM drops the Overall score
results.setup: Flamingo-3B ablation, 5 DEV validation subsets, 4 shots, short schedule; baseline 70.7 vs 62.7
results.note: Overall = mean of benchmark score / Table 1 SotA; absolute change in that average, not relative
results.quote: Interestingly, ﬁne-tuning our pretrained LM also leads to a drop in performance of −8.0%.

results.claim: Training the LM from scratch drops the Overall score
results.setup: Flamingo-3B ablation, same setup; 57.8 vs 70.7
results.quote: If trained from scratch, we observe a large performance de-crease of −12.9%.

results.claim: Removing M3W interleaved data cuts Overall score by more than 17
results.setup: Flamingo-3B ablation; Overall 53.4 without M3W vs 70.7
results.quote: removing the interleaved image-text dataset M3W leads to a decrease of more than 17% in performance

results.claim: Removing image-text pairs cuts Overall score
results.setup: Flamingo-3B ablation; 60.9 vs 70.7 (drop 9.8)
results.quote: removing the conventional paired image-text pairs also decreases
results.table: Table 3, row w/o Image-Text pairs, column Overall

results.claim: Gradient accumulation over datasets beats round-robin
results.setup: Flamingo-3B; round robin Overall 62.9 vs 70.7
results.table: Table 3, row (ii) Round Robin, column Overall

results.claim: Removing zero-initialised tanh gating drops Overall and causes instability
results.setup: Flamingo-3B ablation, Overall 66.5 vs 70.7
results.quote: Without it, we see a drop of 4.2% in our overall score.

results.claim: GATED XATTN-DENSE every 4th block trains 66% faster for 1.9 lower Overall
results.setup: Flamingo-3B ablation; 68.8 vs 70.7, step time 1.02s vs 1.74s
results.quote: inserting them every fourth block accelerates training by 66% while only decreasing the overall score by 1.9%

results.claim: NFNet-F6 vision encoder beats CLIP ViT-L/14
results.setup: Flamingo-3B ablation; 64.9 vs 70.7
results.quote: Our NFNet-F6 has a +5.8% advantage over the CLIP ViT-L/14

results.claim: Cross-attending only to the most recent image beats attending to all previous images
results.setup: Flamingo-3B; 63.5 for all-previous vs 70.7
results.quote: the single image case leads to signiﬁcantly better results (7.2% better in the overall score)

results.claim: Unfreezing vision encoder from scratch drops Overall
results.setup: Flamingo-3B, Table 10 row v; step time 4.70s* with 4x chips
results.quote: the performance decreases by a large margin of −9.3%

results.claim: C4-pretrained frozen LM instead of MassiveText
results.setup: Flamingo-3B, Table 10 row iv

results.claim: Co-training on MassiveText from random init
results.setup: Flamingo-3B, Table 10 row vi; pretrained start gives 68.6, both below 70.7
results.table: Table 10, row (vi) Co-train LM (random init), column Overall

results.claim: Largest model trained on 1536 TPUv4 chips for 15 days
results.setup: Flamingo-80B, sharded across 16 devices
results.quote: is trained on 1536 chips for 15 days

results.claim: RICES beats random example selection on ImageNet
results.setup: Flamingo-80B, 16 of 5000 support examples
results.quote: Flamingo achieves a 9.2% improvement in ImageNet classiﬁcation when selecting 16 support examples out of 5000 using RICES

results.claim: Flamingo-80B with RICES plus ensembling on ImageNet top-1
results.setup: 16 prompt size, 5 shots/class; zero-shot own contrastive model scores 77.9
results.table: Table 7, row Flamingo-80B RICES+ensembling, column ImageNet top 1

results.claim: M3W near-duplicates found against eval sets
results.setup: 185M M3W images; 1314 candidates, 125 exact duplicates
results.quote: Out of the 1314 candidates, only 125 are exact duplicates.

results.claim: Bias study: COCO CIDEr gap female vs male at 32 shots not significant
results.setup: two-tailed t-test unequal variance on per-sample CIDEr; lowest p across four comparisons 0.25
results.quote: the lowest p-value we ﬁnd is 𝑝= 0.25

limits: Inherits LM weaknesses: hallucination, poor length generalisation (VisDial prompts 4096-8192 tokens vs 2048 training length, capped at 16 shots)
Classification lags contrastive models, including its own vision encoder
In-context learning is order- and format-sensitive; performance plateaus beyond 32 shots; inference cost scales with shots
Each model trained once, no error bars; DEV benchmarks biased by model selection
Code, weights and data not released; English only; M3W not deduplicated, VizWiz/HatefulMemes/TextVQA not deduplicated
Preliminary bias study only; 2022 SotA comparisons have dated

terms.definition: takes a variable number of image or video features and produces a fixed number of visual outputs (64) via learned latent queries
Retrieval-based In-Context Example Selection: retrieve similar support images by frozen encoder features
